Engineering notes

Family-level evidence reviewed October 1, 2026. Manufacturer-published data is not independent bench validation. Examples below are not selected inventory SKUs; existing catalog fields are not replaced with family ranges.

Manufacturer specifications

LCS uses a standard cup-shaped flexspline. LCS-I has keyed input; LCS-II uses an Oldham coupling. LCSG is a separate strengthened family. Leaderdrive LCS, Models.

Conditions and revision conflicts

Frame 20, ratio 100 is an example, not a complete SKU. The website table lists rated 40 Nm, start-stop 82 Nm, maximum average load 49 Nm, maximum peak 147 Nm and maximum input 6,500 rpm. The LCS-I manual, PDF page 2 in ZIP instead lists 38 Nm at 2,000 rpm, start-stop 78 Nm, average 47 Nm, momentary 140 Nm and maximum input 6,000 rpm. Rating conditions and applicable revision need confirmation; do not combine them into SKU limits.

Engineering inference

The LCS geometry archive contains STEP and Parasolid geometry. Drawings and source-qualified mechanical tables support partial modeling, not a calibrated dynamics or thermal model.

Inference assumes the selected drawing and applicable revision are confirmed. Confidence in model completeness is low; no numerical efficiency, cooldown or precision estimate is defensible from this evidence.

Unknown / confirmation required

Numerical product-specific efficiency, cooling hardware, repeated thermal duty/derating, externally measured loaded output repeatability and calibrated simulation support remain unconfirmed in the reviewed material. Unknown is not zero. Encoder or sensor resolution is not output accuracy. Motor voltage, current and motor constants are not applicable to a reducer alone; select a motor/drive separately.

Manufacturer specifications

The product page advertises configurator CAD, but no WPG CAD download was verified in this review. Catalog main-bearing moment rigidity is not drivetrain torsional stiffness. Related WPU efficiency charts do not establish WPG efficiency.

Manufacturer specifications

The sensorized WPU-SRH-BD has a cross-roller-supported flange and hollow input for routing; it is not an integrated motor. Nidec SRH. The Smart-FLEXWAVE catalog, pages 4–6 gives frame 50, ratio 100 nominal 52 Nm, start-stop 107 Nm, emergency 191 Nm and life 7,692 hours at 2,000 rpm input and nominal torque. Sensor data lists 12-bit torque resolution, nonlinearity ±3% FS or less and hysteresis 3% FS or less within rated torque. These do not establish total-system accuracy or output-position repeatability. The 24 VDC supply and 3.0 Mbps half-duplex RS-485 are sensor electronics, not a motor bus or servo protocol.

Conditions and revision conflicts

The website lists sensor current ≤0.06 A; the catalog, page 5 lists ≤0.1 A. Both are T.B.D.; final consumption is unknown. Catalog ±2°C temperature accuracy is also T.B.D. Frame 35/42 comparison masses 0.72/1.0 kg differ from dimensions/catalog values 0.78/1.05 kg. Certification prose says obtained while the table retains expected-in-2024 wording: request the certificate and scope rather than infer whole-machine compliance. Compensation notation ±0.05FS/°C lacks an explicit percent sign; do not normalize it.

Engineering inference

Catalog frame-specific mass/inertia and sensing can assist identification, but no calibrated simulator package was verified. The 0–80°C sensor measurement/electronics range is not unrestricted reducer ambient or continuous thermal duty. Temperature monitoring is not cooling; ordinary WPU efficiency charts do not explicitly validate SRH-BD.
